author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
A senior devs of today do not automatically transform into a senior devs of tomorrow.   If they don't learn how to use AI, they will just become obsolete.

The playing field is leveled out by AI, junior dev and senior dev today both are racing to learn how to be the AI senior dev of tomorrow.   Guess who pick up AI faster?

reshared_post.reshared_text:
"If AI kills junior dev jobs, how will we ever get senior devs?"

This is the wrong question. Here's why.

The junior → senior pipeline was never good. Tearing it up is probably the right thing to do.

First, a hard truth: If you're a developer in late 2025 and you still haven't learned AI coding tools, or tried them once and dismissed them as "overhyped", you're displaying a failure of the core skill of software engineering.

That skill isn't writing code. It's learning.

Every project uses a different stack. Tech evolves constantly. New things added, old things replaced... Devs who can't get excited about the biggest shift in our field's history have basically marked themselves as dinosaurs.

But for those paying attention, the worry is real: "How do we get seniors if we tear up the junior/mid pipeline?"

Here's the thing: that pipeline was never good. Tearing it up is probably the right thing to do. The "conveyor belt" was never a good way to train senior devs.

The traditional path looked like this:
1. CS degree
2. Junior dev job
3. Work hard, accrue experience
4. Get promoted to "senior"

I call this the Conveyor Belt. This path produces mediocrity. People who follow it tend to fail at curiosity, excitement, desire to build new things.

AI is slamming the brakes on this path.

The business case for hiring juniors is now zero.

Previously, expanding capacity meant hiring people. Now it means spend more on tokens.

It's cheaper, less hassle, doesn't kill your nimbleness, and gets better every month - unlike junior devs who need years to improve!

But here's what people miss: there's another path. There always was.

But there's another path to becoming a "senior dev"!

The Bootstrap Path: You teach yourself. You build things. You deploy them. You build more things. You learn by doing.

No one needs to spoon-feed you.

YOU CAN JUST DO THINGS!

When I learned to code in the 90s, I took the bus to Geneva's one good IT bookstore, read books I couldn't afford, went home and applied what I learned.

Today there are infinite free resources. YouTube, books, tutorials, LLMs as personal tutors. This is better than ever.

So "how will we train senior software engineers?"

Wrong question.

We won't train them. They will train themselves, or they will do something else.

The era of formal career ladders for devs without the drive to self-teach is over.

This will massively increase the quality of senior engineers.

The Great Filtering is here: everyone who couldn't get excited about the most transformative thing to ever happen to our field will be filtered out.

And only those with the drive to self-teach will be "seniors".
